Trellised garden gates stand open between cottages, rose canes and climbing bean-vines threading every wooden bar in dense green tangles.
Roof ridges are decorated with carved clay birds and acorn finials, painted in earthy reds and soft greens, slightly worn.
Narrow alley passages between the old stone houses are barely wide enough for two, roofed in places by connected balconies above.
Reflecting pools sit still in cottage gardens, ringed with smooth stones, their surfaces scattered with lily-pads and floating white petals.
Lantern-posts of twisted ironwork stand at every corner, their glass chambers fogged and warm, casting soft halos on the wet cobbles.
Arched footbridges with leaf-carved railings span the quiet stream, mossy stones worn smooth by generations of light elven feet.
Warm glowing leaded windows cast amber honeycomb light across the cobbles, flower-boxes spilling sweet alyssum and trailing ivy below.
Cascading wisteria drapes the eaves in curtains of violet and lavender, its perfume drifting lazily through every lantern-lit lane.
Fairy-lanterns strung between the cottages sway gently on copper wire, their soft golden glow pulsing like slow, contented breath.
Mushrooms of russet and cream nestle against every doorstep, tucked among clover and moss as though they always belonged there.
Spiral stone stairs wind up the outer walls of the smallest turrets, each step edged with lichen and tiny white flowers.
Tiny iron balconies draped with fern and trailing vine overlook the cobbled square, candles flickering in little glass-paned lanterns beside the doors.
Glowing vines climb the castle turrets, their leaves veined with soft bioluminescent light that brightens as the evening deepens around them.
Cobbled paths wind between the cottages in gentle curves, each stone fitted with patient elven care, moss filling every seam.
Little waterwheels turn lazily on the mill-stream, their paddles painted in faded blue and green, dripping silver in the afternoon light.
Mossy roofs thick with creeping thyme and stonecrop give every cottage the look of a hill that simply decided to have a door.
Chimneys of pale river-stone release curling threads of fragrant smoke, scented with cedar and dried lavender from the hearths below.
Wind-chimes of sea-green and amber glass hang from every porch beam, filling the lanes with soft, ringing music at the slightest breeze.
Hanging baskets overflow with nasturtium, sweet pea, and trailing lobelia, suspended from wrought-iron hooks shaped like curling fern fronds.
Carved wooden shutters painted sage and cream frame each window, their panels etched with running deer and spiraling leaf-work.
A communal well sits at the village center, its stone collar wound with climbing roses and its bucket-chain wrought in the shape of braided vines.
Thatched eaves extend low over the doorways, fringed with dried flowers and small bundles of herbs tied with faded ribbon.
Elven-blown glass orbs nestle in the garden beds, catching the light and scattering small rainbows across the white cottage walls beside them.
Narrow alley-ways between the houses are roofed in wisteria and climbing rose, forming fragrant green tunnels lit by strung lanterns overhead.
Stone window seats built into the cottage walls hold cushions of embroidered linen, just wide enough for a cup of tea and a small cat.
Dovecotes of pale timber stand at the corners of the village green, their occupants cooing softly amid a flutter of silver-white wings.
Garden gates of bent willow-branch and copper wire stand open at every path, wrapped in honeysuckle and starred with tiny bell-flowers.
A great oak at the village heart has a door set into its trunk and a lamp hung in its first fork, burning all night.
Stepping-stone paths cross the small kitchen gardens, each stone painted with a single flower or creature, worn to a gentle gleam with years of use.
Arched footbridges with leaf-carved railings cross the glittering streams, their mossy stones worn smooth by centuries of elven feet.
Warm glowing leaded windows spill amber light onto the cobbles, flower-boxes beneath them overflowing with moon-kissed blossoms and trailing vines.
Wisteria cascades in thick lavender curtains over the eaves, filling the laneway with sweetness and soft drifting petals at dusk.
Fairy-lanterns strung between the cottages sway gently in the evening breeze, casting pools of gold and rose across the cobblestones.
Mushrooms of every speckled variety tuck themselves against doorsteps and garden walls, glowing faintly with a quiet enchantment after nightfall.
Spiral stairs of pale stone wind up the cottage towers, their banisters wound with flowering vine and tiny silver bells.
Glowing vines climb the turrets in slow spiraling coils, their leaves luminous at the edges as though lit from within.
Cobbled paths wind between the little houses in gentle curves, each stone fitted with elvish care, moss filling every seam.
Little waterwheels turn lazily beside the mill-stream, painted with faded flower motifs, their paddles green with cheerful river moss.
